item.title: Judge blocks plan to return Trump's name to the Kennedy Center
item.description: The judge ruled that the arts center's board may not put Trump's name back up on the building, saying such a change needs Congressional approval.
item.content:encoded:

item.title: Republican Rep. Massie moves to impeach Defense Secretary Hegseth over Iran war
item.description: Kentucky Republican Thomas Massie introduced articles of impeachment against Secretary of Defense Pete Hegseth on Tuesday over the war in Iran.

item.title: Trump says developing AI is a critical race, downplaying fears
item.description: President Trump continues to support frontier artificial intelligence development, despite industry fears such technology could destroy humanity, casting AI as a critical race against China.

item.description: NPR's Leila Fadel speaks with U.S. Sen. Bernie Sanders,I-Vermont, about his concerns over the risks of artificial intelligence.

item.title: This bill could reshape crypto in America -- and it's sparking a major battle
item.description: The legislation would establish rules of the road for the crypto sector for the first time — but opponents are up in arms, and the bill faces an uncertain prospect in the Senate.

item.title: Bernie Sanders and Steve Bannon call for curbs on AI
item.description: The rare pairing of a progressive leader and a MAGA voice is a sign of how worries over rapidly advancing AI are upending political alliances. But their policy proposals are far apart.

item.title: The Supreme Court rejects Trump's mail voting restrictions for this year's midterms
item.description: The Supreme Court has rejected the Trump administration's request to allow mail-in voting restrictions under a U.S. Postal Service plan for the midterm general election.

item.description: McConnell spent weeks in recovery before explaining he was "briefly unconscious" following the fall that sent him to the hospital and a weeks-long recovery process.

item.title: Federal agents may have broken state laws in voter fraud hunt, whistleblower claims
item.description: Federal agents may have broken state laws after the Department of Homeland Security began surging personnel for what it called the Unlawful Voter Initiative, a federal whistleblower alleges.
